thread.title: How To Prepare Your Portfolio For A Trade War

author: Ken Kam
title: How To Prepare Your Portfolio For A Trade War
text:
Share to twitter Share to linkedin A trade war with China, Europe, Canada, and Mexico changes the outlook for many stocks. and research what to buy if the market corrects after the next round of tariffs is announced. Nate Pile, a Marketocracy manager who has beaten the market for over 15 years, is selling some Apple and Nvidia to raise cash to buy biotech.
Ken Kam: Nate, you have been trading more than usual lately. What is motivating this?
Nate Pile: As you know, I have been skeptical of President Trump’s decision to go down the road of trade wars as part of implementing his economic vision. But, I was willing to wait and see if the “big talk” would have the desired effect of bringing about productive conversations across the negotiating table.
However, it has become clear that either a trade war with the rest of the world is what was actually intended in the first place or we have to accept the fact that Trump and his team may be losing control of the situation. Neither of these possibilities are the sorts of foundations upon which a healthy global economy can be built and maintained.
Kam: So how are you changing your porftolio?
Pile: With any eye towards winding up with roughly a 5% cash position, I am selling between 10–20% of our positions in those stocks that I believe may be hit the hardest as part of a trade war, and, on the buy side, I am increasing our stake in biotech on hopes that the rally that appears to be getting underway in biotech is “for real”. MannKind Mannkind Corp and the company's inhalable insulin product. Development associate Punam Patel preparing samples for analysis in the company's research facilities in Valencia. (Photo by Lawrence K. Ho/Los Angeles Times via Getty Images)
I am very pleased to report that Mike Castagna, MannKind’s CEO, has decided the time is right launch a fairly aggressive marketing campaign. The company is now running Afrezza TV ads on a wide variety of networks and programming-styles (news, game shows, etc.) in a rather impressive number of regions around the country. The variety of demographics it is aimed at ought to go a long ways towards addressing the “awareness” piece of the puzzle that has been cited by many as a reason scripts haven’t been ramping faster.
In addition, now that additional studies have been released, MannKind’s sales reps can finally start talking about the benefits of Afrezza that those of us in the real world have known about anecdotally for several years now.
Now that all the pieces are in place to market the real benefits of Afrezza, we will soon get an accurate gauge of Afrezza’s commercial potential. If we do not see a significant improvement in sales over the next six to twelve months, I will have no choice but to start re-evaluating my outlook.
My current plan is to make one last sizable purchase this month then sit tight through August and September, and then make a decision about what to do next based on how the trend in scripts is looking.
No, we’re not out of the woods yet. But after all the work Castagna and his team have done over the past eighteen months, Afrezza is proving to be all it was cracked up to be, and, at least so far, Castagna & Co. have done nothing but demonstrate that they’ve got what it will take to see things through and make MannKind very successful.
MNKD is a strong buy under $5 and a buy under $10. Nvidia Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. (Photo credit MANDEL NGAN/AFP/Getty Images)
Nvidia took a bit of a tumble a month ago, traded sideways for a bit, and has since started the process of trying to bounce off that support level. Although the longer-term trend is still pretty clearly “up,” I have to admit that between the trade war and the fact that the stock has already gone up ten-fold from where it was just two-and-a-half years ago, Nvidia is thus ripe for some profit-taking.
I will grow much more bearish if Nvidia happens to fall below $210 in the months ahead (and much more bullish if it clears $270 instead!). NVDA remains a strong buy under $240 and a buy under $265. Apple Apple CEO Tim Cook. (Photo by Justin Sullivan/Getty Images)
Despite the fact that Apple is clearly a company that has a lot riding on the outcome of a trade war, the stock has actually held up very well in recent weeks. In fact, Apple is once again sitting within striking distance of a new all-time high and that psychologically huge $1 trillion market cap.
What the company has to say about the trade situation in its upcoming earnings call will likely help set the tone for the market going forward. As mentioned earlier, my decision to sell roughly 10% of my position this month is being done simply to raise our cash level. AAPL remains a strong buy under $180 and a buy under $200. My Take
It takes courage to stick with a stock that drops 90% after you buy it. This level of confidence is only warranted when the manager has an exceptionally strong track record. Long time subscribers to his newsletter, Nates Notes , know that MannKind is not Nate’s first roller coaster.
Nate recommended Celgene in 1995 when it had a market cap of just $87 million. For years, Celgene bounced around a split adjusted 20 cents and 50 cents as all of the skeptics on Wall Street openly mocked the company's plan to market a product with a "black box warning" on the label with no marketing partner. Today Celgene trades at $86 and it's market cap is $62 Billion.
In June of 1998, Nate recommended Apple (then at $1.50) when its market share was in the single digits, cash was running low, and bankruptcy was a real possibility. Today Apple is at $190.
Over the more than 15 years, I've tracked his performance, Nate Pile has averaged 17.77% a year which compares well to the S&P 500s 9.84% for the same period. One hallmark of his skill is that no matter how much he is convinced of a stocks potential, he does not let it get to be such a large position that it would be a disaster if he turned out to be wrong.
